findings.description: CARRY-FORWARD OWNERSHIP IS CONTRADICTED BY THE CODE. Spec: "`runtime` owns carry-forward, retaining the last cached marks" — stated unconditionally. Code: carry-forward lives in TWO places. `sheets-view::read_marks` takes `prior: &BTreeMap<Symbol, Mark>` and, for any symbol that reads `Transient` OR is absent from the pass after the bounded window, re-emits the prior mark into THIS cycle's `out.marks` and does NOT record it degraded (lib.rs:873-879 `if let Some(prev) = prior.get(s) { out.marks.insert(s.clone(), *prev) }`); test `transient_keeps_prior_mark_and_retries_degrades_only_after_window` (marks.rs:162-191) pins the stale `Cents(180_00)` / `Date(19_100)` mark being emitted as this cycle's mark with `degraded` empty. Both directions hit this from opposite sides: all 3 A-runs, reading the ownership clause, built a STATELESS reader with no `prior` parameter at all (A2 assumption 9: "Runtime holds cache; sheets-view is stateless — no last-good copy kept here"; A1 assumption 6: "this function is pure and holds no cache reference, which is what makes carry-forward structurally `runtime`-owned"); all 3 B-runs report `prior` and the transient carry as code-enforced. Consequence a cold reader of 006 cannot see: a stale price with a stale `quote_date` is silently republished as the live mark. Caveat: a sibling SHEET-MARK spec may own the transient path, but 006's ownership sentence reads false as written.

THE TRANSPORT-FAILURE GUARD IS BYPASSED BY THE MISSING-TAB / EMPTY-PASS DOOR — a classification boundary the spec never states. The code's only definition of "transport failure" is `Err` from `read_price_pass`. `runtime::adapters::ViewSheetsAdapter::read_price_pass` (adapters.rs:262-265) matches `Err(ref e) if is_missing_tab(e) => Vec::new()` and returns `Ok(empty PricePass)`; cold_start.rs pins it (`the_price_pass_on_a_fresh_workbook_is_empty_not_an_error`, plus `the_missing_tab_400_classifies_as_tab_missing_not_unreachable` / `an_offline_workbook_still_classifies_as_unreachable` for the 400 `Unable to parse range` vs `StoreError::Unreachable` split). An empty `Ok` pass drives `read_marks` through the `None` arm for EVERY symbol: it burns all `max_polls` (default 8) polls without settling, then degrades every prior-less symbol `DegradeReason::TimedOut` with no mark, and `to_ledger_marks()` omits them so replay nulls every unrealized. That is precisely the "all symbols degraded, wrongly nulling live positions" outcome the code's own doc comment (lib.rs:806-816) says the loud propagation exists to prevent — reached through a path 006 never mentions and no test covers. All 3 B-runs surfaced the missing-tab-is-not-an-outage rule; the spec text contains nothing about it.

"NO PARTIAL ... MARKS" IS NOT ENFORCED AGAINST A PARTIAL SUCCESSFUL READ — there is no completeness gate. Spec forbids partial marks for the pass. Code: `read_marks` treats a symbol absent from the returned `PricePass` identically to `Transient` (settled check at lib.rs:836-838 `!matches!(latest.get(s), Some(PriceReading::Transient) | None)`, and the merged `Some(Transient) | None` arm at lib.rs:873), so a short/truncated read silently becomes per-symbol carry-or-degrade and returns `Ok` — a genuinely partial marks set. All 3 A-runs raised this from the spec text: A1 and A2 both implemented an explicit gate (`if buf.len() != expected.len() { return Err(... format!("short read: {} of {}", ...)) }`) and A3 flagged it explicitly ("`tickers`/`cells` length mismatch is not handled explicitly; `zip` truncates. A real implementation should make that a hard error"). The real code has neither the gate nor a test for a pass that covers only some requested symbols.

`republish_then_settle` DISCARDS THE ALREADY-COMMITTED `RepublishOutcome` ON A SETTLE-HALF TRANSPORT FAILURE. Code (lib.rs:1021-1023): `let outcome = self.republish(tabs, lock, stale_banner_quote_ts); let marks = read_marks(&self.client, symbols, prior, cfg)?;` — the `?` throws `outcome` away even though the per-tab `batchUpdate`s already landed in the workbook and `Publisher.stale` was already mutated (tabs inserted/removed, stale banners written). The caller gets only the `ViewError` and cannot learn which tabs published or which are now flagged stale, while the workbook state has genuinely changed. Spec 006 scopes its rule to "that pass" and says nothing about the combined republish-then-settle cycle; all 3 B-runs independently flagged the discarded outcome and the un-rolled-back write. Untested (no test drives a read failure through `republish_then_settle`).

"PROPAGATE THE ERROR" COLLAPSES ONTO `ViewError::PublishFailed` — the transport failure loses its identity. `ViewError` has exactly three variants: `PublishFailed | SettleTimeout | DuplicateSymbolRow` (lib.rs:399-413) — no transport/unreachable variant. Both the real adapter (adapters.rs:264 `r => r.map_err(|_| sheets_view::ViewError::PublishFailed)?`) and the testkit (testkit.rs:206-208 `if *self.read_fails.borrow() { return Err(ViewError::PublishFailed) }`) surface a settle-pass READ failure under the variant named for the WRITE path, so a `republish_then_settle` caller cannot tell whether the publish half or the read-back half failed. The sole transport test (marks.rs:132-159) asserts only `result.is_err()`, never which variant. Direction A: all 3 runs modeled a dedicated, distinguishable `MarksError::Transport` variant on the strength of "propagate THE error". Direction B: B1 and B2 both asserted a "transport-class `ViewError` distinct from `ViewError::SettleTimeout`" that does not exist in the code — the B-side reconstructed the intent the naming implies rather than the aliasing the code performs, which is itself evidence the collapse is invisible at the call site.

A TRANSPORT FAILURE IS NEVER RETRIED, WHILE CELL TRANSIENCE IS RETRIED UP TO `SettleConfig.max_polls` (default 8) — and the abort scope is the whole settle window, not one poll. The `?` sits inside the poll loop (lib.rs:828 `let pass = client.read_price_pass()?;`), so an error at ANY poll index aborts immediately and discards every reading accumulated by the earlier successful polls of that same window. The spec says only "propagate the error" and "for that pass": it never states that the bounded retry window applies to `#N/A`/`Loading…` readings but not to transport errors, nor that "pass" means the entire bounded settle window rather than a single poll. A3 independently flagged the scoping ambiguity ("'for that pass' scopes atomicity to a single read-back pass, not to the whole publish cycle"); all 3 B-runs pinned the immediate first-poll abort. No test exercises a transport failure at poll N>1 — `set_read_fails(true)` fails from poll 1, so the discard-accumulated-readings behavior is entirely unpinned.

THE `runtime`-SIDE CLAUSE IS SPEC-STATED BUT ONLY STRUCTURALLY PINNED, AND THE NO-CACHE COLD START IS LEFT OPEN. "retaining the last cached marks" presupposes a cache exists and implies re-injection. Code: `run_cycle(logs, prior: &MarksCache, …) -> Result<CycleOutcome, ViewError>` (cycle.rs:334) propagates the `Err` and simply never mutates `prior` — retention is a consequence of taking a shared reference, not an implemented behavior. The only test, `offline_read_back_propagates_so_caller_retains_prior_marks` (runtime/tests/cycle.rs:308-338), asserts `result.is_err()` and then that the caller's own local `prior.marks["AMZN"]` is still `Cents(160_00)` — trivially true for a `&`-borrowed value; nothing asserts the retained marks are re-injected into the next replay. On a first cycle with `MarksCache::new()` there is nothing to retain and the caller must fall back to `replay_with_cached_marks` with empty marks (every unrealized `None`); the spec is silent on that case. A3 alone raised it (1/3): "The EARS says 'retaining the last cached marks' and is silent when there are none."

notes:
Files read for verification beyond the three named: {scratch}/audit-baseline/crates/sheets-view/src/testkit.rs (line 206-208, the fake's transport error), .../crates/runtime/src/adapters.rs (lines 248-276, the real read_price_pass and its is_missing_tab / PublishFailed mapping), .../crates/runtime/src/cycle.rs (lines 60-115, 300-360, MarksCache + run_cycle), .../crates/runtime/tests/cycle.rs (lines 307-338, the offline propagation test).

CLASSIFICATION RATIONALE (BD-DRIFT): both directions carry material surplus and two of the top findings are the same gap seen from opposite ends. The carry-forward ownership clause is the clearest BD: the A-runs OMITTED the `prior` parameter entirely because the spec assigns carry-forward to `runtime`, while the B-runs REPORTED `prior` and the transient prior-carry as code-enforced. The error-identity finding is likewise bidirectional — A invented a distinct Transport variant from "propagate the error", B asserted one exists, and the code has neither (everything maps to `ViewError::PublishFailed`). Pure-B surplus (missing-tab classification, discarded RepublishOutcome, no-retry-on-transport) and pure-A surplus (no completeness gate, cold-start silence) are both present on top of that.

ASSUMPTION ARTIFACT EXCLUDED, WITH A CAVEAT: all 3 A-runs extended pass-level atomicity to non-transport cell defects (unparseable / `#N/A` / `#ERROR!` fails the whole pass), which the real code contradicts — it degrades per-symbol (`DegradeReason::TimedOut` / `Permanent` / `SubCent`) and returns `Ok` with a mixed marks+degraded set. All three explicitly labeled this an invention beyond the spec's transport scope (A1 #4, A2 #5, A3 #2), so I did not file it as a finding. It nonetheless flags a vocabulary problem worth noting to the spec author: 006's parenthetical "(no partial or degraded marks)" borrows "degraded" from a taxonomy the spec text never introduces, and the code emits partial-and-degraded marks as the NORMAL non-transport outcome — so a cold reader reliably infers the opposite system. Three independent readers made the same wrong inference; that is signal even though it is not a code defect.

SCOPING CAVEAT: SHEET-MARK-006 is one member of a SHEET-MARK-* set. Findings 1 (transient prior-carry) and 6 (max_polls window) touch behavior that sibling specs may legitimately own; they are filed because 006's own text makes unconditional claims ("`runtime` owns carry-forward") or leaves its own scope ("for that pass") undefined, not merely because the neighboring machinery is unstated here. Findings 2, 3, 4, 5 and 7 are not plausibly covered elsewhere in the marks set — they concern the transport path itself.

B-SIDE OVER-READ WORTH FLAGGING TO THE PROTOCOL: B1's SHEET-MARK-TRANSPORT-005 and B2's SHEET-MARK-ERR-007 both assert a "transport-class `ViewError` distinct from `ViewError::SettleTimeout`". No such variant exists; the enum is `PublishFailed | SettleTimeout | DuplicateSymbolRow` and every transport read failure becomes `PublishFailed`. B3 was more careful ("propagate that `ViewError` unchanged"). This is the only substantive disagreement inside direction B and it does not lower the agreement rating — the three reconstructions are otherwise near-identical in content and often in phrasing — but it means B1/B2's error-taxonomy line should be read as intent inferred from naming, not behavior read from code.
